notes: Prostitution-procurement prosecution; boarding/rooming houses mentioned only as incidental waypoints in witness travel testimony, not at issue.
Timber-sale and mill-improvement removal-rights dispute; license/property-affixed-to-land discussion concerns sawmill fixtures, not dwelling occupancy.
Gambling-house/vagrancy statutory-repeal case; defendant's rented family residence used for gaming, not compensated lodging.

quotes.text: his arrangements being that he was given a lower rate than that of a transient guest, but the rate charged roomers, and paid his bills usually once each month, “while transient guests paid each day, or at the end of each week.”

In Kieffer v. Keough (Tex. Civ. App.) 188 S. W. 44, the Galveston Court gives an extended review of the authorities, showing the modern trend of decision to abrogate the early common-law distinction between a guest and a boarder.

notes: Doctrinally on-point for lodger/boarder characterization in a commercial hotel setting, but the holding reduces (not enforces) protections for the occupant, so it does not cleanly fit the favorable/adverse polarity as defined for the corpus; coded mixed.
Habeas challenge to statute criminalizing nighttime removal of a 'laborer or tenant' from a plantation; concerns agricultural tenancy/labor mobility, not room/dwelling lodging.
Venue/plea-of-privilege dispute over defendant's 'residence' vs 'transient' status; mention of renting a furnished house/apartment is background to a domicile analysis only.
Municipal ordinance licensing/locating tent shows and carnivals; police-power zoning analysis, unrelated to dwelling lodging or boarding houses.

Dispute between lessees over advertising-sign rights in a shared hallway (theater vs. 'Page Hotel' apartments upstairs); a leasehold/easement fixture case, not about the character or regulation of the lodging use itself.
Zoning ordinance restricting private meat markets near a city market house; no connection to residential lodging or boarding houses.
Homestead-exemption dispute over crops raised under a farm cropping/leasing arrangement; the landlord/tenant analysis concerns agricultural land, not room or dwelling lodging.

Injunction over a private-garage setback ordinance violation; defendant's property is described in passing as a 'boarding and rooming house,' but the dispute concerns garage placement, not the lodging use or its regulation.
Ordinance restricting motion-picture theaters in residence districts, struck down as an unconstrained delegation of discretion; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

holding_summary: The Court of Civil Appeals held that an automobile tourist camp is not a nuisance per se, that a landowner has the right to use his property for such a lawful business so long as it does not impair the use others make of their own property, and that a petition alleging only anticipated noise, odors, and unsightliness was insufficient, absent facts showing a nuisance would inevitably result, to enjoin construction of the camp buildings in a residence district.

quotes.text: Automobile tourist camp in city or town is not a nuisance as a matter of law.
Owner of land has right to the use of his property so long as such use does not impair or destroy the use of others in their property.

It cannot be held as a matter of law that a camp for the use of travelers by automobile is a nuisance. The use of land for the purpose of a camp in a city or town is a lawful use, and may be exercised without thereby creating a nuisance.

notes: Analogous short-term-lodging authority: court protects a commercial operator's right to house transient travelers overnight against a neighbor's attempt to enjoin the business as a nuisance in a residential district.

Physician-licensing 'residence' registration prosecution; the fact that defendant rented furnished rooms from a householder is used only to establish domicile for the registration statute, not to characterize the lodging arrangement itself.

Sheriff-liability/homestead-abandonment case; owner rented out an entire former-residence house on his lot for continuous income over two years — a long-term whole-house tenancy for homestead-exemption purposes, not short-term room lodging or boarding-house regulation.
Murder appeal; defendant's flight to a friend's 'lodging house' after the killing is mentioned only in an evidentiary-error analysis, not at issue as a lodging arrangement.
Ordinance defining and abating public dance halls in residence districts as nuisances; entertainment-venue police-power case, not lodging.
Conversion suit turning on whether a landlord's lien for farm supplies attached to cotton crops; agricultural share-cropping/landlord-tenant dispute unrelated to dwelling lodging.
